children: UK public sector net borrowing figures for August are due to be released at a time of “intense volatility” for the UK gilt market, according to Kathleen Brooks, research director at

. “Concerns are growing about the rate of UK government borrowing, and the lack of effort to rein in spending,” she said. “The IMF is speaking out about this on a global scale, but the UK is at the forefront of concerns about highly-indebted nations.”
The August data is expected to show that borrowing jumped by £15.7bn in one month, pushing up net debt as a proportion of GDP. It currently it stands at 94.1%.
On the corporate front, all eyes will be on retailer Kingfisher, the blue-chip owner of B&Q, Screwfix and Europe’s Castorama, and how it fared over the key spring season.

noted: “Tough prior year comparatives and a late start to spring dented the DIY group’s first quarter like-for-like ales growth despite Screwfix continuing to take market share in trade. Nevertheless [Kingfisher] stuck with full-year guidance, which implies management confidence of returning to positive like-for-like sales growth on the back of a recovery in big ticket purchases.”
